### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14, A15, A20 and A21 are not observed at all (0 of 200 cases), while A23, A24 and A25 occur in every case and always run directly in sequence: A23 is followed by A24 one step later, A24 by A25 one step later, and A23 and A25 are always two steps apart. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

- In the later window, these four activities appear for the first time: A14 in about 24 of 100 cases, A15 in about 21, A20 in about 31 and A21 in about 25, each at most once per case. No case contains two of them, and together they occur in about 199 of 200 later cases. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL009, REL010, REL016]

- In the later window, each of the four always occurs after A23 and before A25, and its own outgoing transitions split roughly evenly between A24 and A25 (for example A15: about 61 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A24, about 39 to A25). [REL004, REL006, REL011, REL013, REL017, REL019, REL022, REL024, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

- Routing around the original chain redistributed: A23's outgoing transitions, previously all to A24, now go about 49 in 100 to A24 and about 51 in 100 to one of the four activities; A24's, previously all to A25, now go about 52 in 100 to A25 and about 48 in 100 to one of the four. A23, A24 and A25 themselves still occur in every later case. [DIR005, DIR006]

- Successive gaps widened by one step in about half of the later cases: A23 to A24 is two steps apart in about 51 of 100 later cases (previously always 1), A24 to A25 in about 49 of 100 (previously always 1), and A23 to A25 in about 995 of 1000 (previously always 2). [LAG001, LAG003, LAG002]

- A39, present in about 72 of 100 earlier cases, appears in only about 56 of 100 later cases; the four activities co-occur with A39 in about 12–17 of 100 cases each and occur without it in about 8–14 of 100. When they occur, the four activities sit near the middle of the case (mean relative position about 0.5). [REL008, REL015, REL021, REL026, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, one of four mutually exclusive activities — A14, A15, A20 or A21 — occurs in nearly every case between A23 and A25, placed before A24 in about half of the cases and after A24 in the other half, whereas earlier A23, A24 and A25 always ran directly in sequence. This rests on direct relational and positional evidence, not just frequency counts: each of the four always lies after A23 and before A25; the outgoing transitions of A23 and A24 shifted exactly at their former edges; and all three measured successions (A23→A24, A24→A25, A23→A25) moved by exactly one step. The amount of evidence also exceeds what an unchanged process typically yields: 43 items qualified from 103 tested units against roughly 0.5 expected by chance, and every item's difference is larger than in 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL004, REL006, REL011, REL013, REL017, REL019, REL022, REL024, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL009, REL010, REL016, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: the many relation items largely restate the same underlying behaviour for the four activities and are not independent confirmations; with two finite 200-case samples, sampling differences in variant frequencies cannot be strictly excluded, although 0 of 200 earlier versus about 199 of 200 later makes a pure sampling explanation implausible. The evidence also does not show what determines the choice among the four activities or between the two positions, and the accompanying drop in A39 (about 72 to about 56 of 100 cases) is not accounted for by this reading and may be a separate difference. [REL008, REL015, REL021, REL026]

Now let's understand the behavioural pattern.

OCC items: A14, A15, A20, A21 all have zero participation before, and after: A14 0.24 (48/200), A15 0.205 (41/200), A20 0.305 (61/200), A21 0.245 (49/200).
